subject.title: [Bug] v2026.6.9 QQBot: long markdown reply is split into N independent bubbles (one per chunk), not a single message

question: Should QQBot keep proactive Markdown chunking as the intended delivery contract, or should safe-size chunks be merged into one QQ message bubble when the merged payload is within the verified QQ limit?
rationale: Current source and the latest release still send one QQ API message per planned chunk, sliverp says that is intentional to avoid truncation, and an open PR proposes changing the user-visible contract for safe-size chunks.

options.title: Accept bounded safe merging
options.body: Review and land the linked PR only if live QQ C2C proof confirms merged safe-size replies render as one bubble and oversized replies still split without duplicate or lost delivery.

options.title: Keep chunking by design
options.body: Close this issue and the linked merge PR after documenting that QQBot preserves Markdown correctness by splitting long replies before QQ truncation can break formatting.

options.title: Add explicit channel policy
options.body: Expose or document a QQBot-owned delivery policy so users can choose between fewer bubbles and strict anti-truncation behavior without changing defaults silently.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded safe merging
recommendation.body: Review and land the linked PR only if live QQ C2C proof confirms merged safe-size replies render as one bubble and oversized replies still split without duplicate or lost delivery.

likelyOwner.reason: sliverp has the strongest QQBot Markdown history and already stated the current product rationale on the issue.
